question: Before loading or unloading hazardous materials, what must a driver do to the vehicle?
choice_a: Turn on the four-way flashers only
choice_b: Disconnect the trailer from the tractor
choice_d: Set the parking brake to make sure the vehicle will not move
explanation: Before loading or unloading, set the parking brake and make sure the vehicle will not move.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-10

question: What must a driver do before loading or unloading Class 1 explosives?
choice_a: Turn on the cargo heater to keep the space dry
choice_b: Turn off the engine
choice_d: Set the cruise control
explanation: Turn your engine off before loading or unloading any explosives, then check the cargo space, disable cargo heaters, and check for sharp points that could damage cargo.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-10

question: For Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, what type of floor lining is required if one is used?
choice_a: Any metal, including stainless steel
choice_b: Untreated plywood only
choice_c: Either non-metallic material or non-ferrous metal
choice_d: Galvanized steel sheeting
explanation: The floors must be tight and the liner must be either non-metallic material or non-ferrous metal (metal that does not contain iron or iron alloys).
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-10

question: What should you do if a package of explosives shows any dampness or an oily stain?
choice_a: Wrap it in an extra tarp and load it
choice_b: Never transport it
choice_c: Wipe it off and load it as usual
choice_d: Load it last, farthest from the cab
explanation: The manual instructs: 'Never transport damaged packages of explosives. Do not take a package that shows any dampness or oily stain.'
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-10

question: Class 4 and 5 materials that become unstable and dangerous when wet must be handled how during loading, unloading, and transit?
choice_a: Stored in an open, uncovered trailer
choice_b: Lightly misted with water to reduce dust
choice_d: Kept dry at all times
explanation: Class 4 and 5 materials that become unstable and dangerous when wet must be kept dry while in transit and during loading and unloading.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-11

question: When loading breakable containers of corrosive liquid by hand, how should they be handled?
choice_a: Load them one by one, right side up, without dropping or rolling them
choice_b: Load several at once using a hand truck without regard to orientation
choice_c: Roll them gently to the loading position
choice_d: Stack them on their sides to save space
explanation: If loading corrosive liquid containers by hand, load them one by one, keep them right side up, and do not drop or roll them; stack carboys only if lower tiers can bear the weight of upper tiers.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-11

question: According to the loading rules, nitric acid must never be loaded in which position?
choice_a: Above any other product
choice_b: In the front of the trailer
choice_d: Next to the fuel tank
explanation: The manual states: 'Do not load nitric acid above any other product.'
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-11

question: If a vehicle carrying compressed gas cylinders has no racks to hold them, cylinders may be loaded horizontally only if:
choice_a: They are loaded on top of other freight
choice_b: The cylinders are wrapped in blankets
choice_c: The trailer has a lift gate
choice_d: It is designed so the relief valve is in the vapor space
explanation: Cylinders may be loaded in a horizontal position (lying down) if designed so the relief valve is in the vapor space; otherwise they must be held upright or in racks/boxes that prevent turning over.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-11

question: What is the maximum total transport index allowed for all Class 7 (Radioactive) packages in a single vehicle?
explanation: The manual states 'The total transport index of all packages in a single vehicle must not exceed 50.'
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-12

question: According to the Do Not Load table, Division 6.1 or 2.3 (poison or poison inhalation hazard labeled material) generally must not be loaded in the same vehicle with what?
choice_a: Empty pallets
choice_b: Spare tires
choice_c: Animal or human food, unless the poison package is over packed in an approved way
choice_d: Non-hazardous dry goods
explanation: The Do Not Load table lists Division 6.1 or 2.3 poison-labeled material as not to be loaded with animal or human food unless the poison package is over packed in an approved way.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-12

question: When loading or unloading, near which of these hazard classes must smoking never be allowed?
choice_a: Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), Class 3 (Flammable Liquids), Class 4 (Flammable Solids), and Class 5 (Oxidizers)
choice_b: ORM-D materials only
choice_d: Class 9 (Miscellaneous) only
explanation: The manual lists Class 1, Class 2.1, Class 3, Class 4, and Class 5 as classes around which smoking and open fire are never allowed during loading or unloading.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-9

question: What is the required color and size for identification numbers displayed on placards, orange panels, or white diamond backgrounds on cargo tanks?
choice_a: Black, 100 mm (3.9 inches)
choice_b: Blue, 150 mm (6 inches)
choice_d: Red, 50 mm (2 inches)
explanation: The rules require black 100 mm (3.9 inch) numbers on orange panels, placards, or a white, diamond-shaped background if no placards are required.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-12

question: On a portable tank with a capacity of more than 1,000 gallons, how tall must the letters of the shipping name marking be?
choice_a: At least two inches tall
choice_b: No minimum height is specified
choice_d: At least one-half inch tall
explanation: The letters of the shipping name must be at least two inches tall on portable tanks with capacities of more than 1,000 gallons and one-inch tall on portable tanks with capacities of less than 1,000 gallons.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-12

question: While a cargo tank is being loaded or unloaded, how far away may the qualified person watching it be?
choice_a: Within 100 feet, out of sight is acceptable
choice_b: Anywhere on the property
choice_c: At least 50 feet away, for safety
choice_d: Within 25 feet of the tank, with a clear view
explanation: The person watching the loading or unloading must be alert, have a clear view of the cargo tank, and be within 25 feet of the tank, among other requirements.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-12

question: Is it legal to move a cargo tank with open valves or covers?
choice_a: Yes, if the tank is nearly empty
choice_b: Yes, as long as the driver has a hazmat endorsement
choice_c: It is illegal, unless the tank is empty according to 49 CFR 173.29
choice_d: Yes, if moving less than one mile
explanation: Close all manholes and valves before moving a tank of hazardous materials; it is illegal to move a cargo tank with open valves or covers unless it is empty according to 49 CFR 173.29.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-12

question: Before filling a cargo tank with a flammable liquid through an open filling hole, what must the driver do to the tank?
choice_a: Disconnect the parking brake
choice_b: Paint the fill port a bright color
choice_c: Fill it as quickly as possible to reduce vapor buildup
choice_d: Ground the tank correctly before opening the filling hole
explanation: Turn off your engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids, and ground a cargo tank correctly before filling it through an open filling hole.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-13

question: Liquid discharge valves on a compressed gas tank should be kept in what condition?
choice_a: Half-open during transit
choice_b: Always open for pressure relief
choice_c: Closed, except when loading and unloading
choice_d: Open only at night
explanation: Keep liquid discharge valves on a compressed gas tank closed except when loading and unloading.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-13

question: How close to the traveled part of the road may you park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives?
choice_a: Never within fifty feet
choice_b: Never within five feet of the traveled part of the road
choice_d: As close as needed, if hazard lights are on
explanation: Never park with Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within five feet of the traveled part of the road.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-13

question: Except for short periods needed for vehicle operation, how close may a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives park to a bridge, tunnel, or place where people gather?
choice_a: There is no restriction if the driver stays with the vehicle
choice_b: No closer than 1,000 feet
choice_d: No closer than 50 feet
explanation: Except for short periods of time needed for vehicle operation necessities, do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, building, a place where people gather, or an open fire.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-13

question: What is a "safe haven" in the context of parking explosives-laden vehicles?
choice_a: An approved place for parking unattended vehicles loaded with explosives
choice_b: Any location more than one mile from a school
choice_d: A designated truck stop restaurant
explanation: A safe haven is an approved place for parking unattended vehicles loaded with explosives, usually designated by local authorities.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-13

question: A person attending a parked placarded vehicle must be in the vehicle, awake, and not in the sleeper berth, or:
choice_a: In a following escort vehicle
choice_b: At a nearby diner having a meal
choice_c: Within 100 feet of the vehicle and have it within clear view
choice_d: Within a quarter mile and reachable by phone
explanation: The person attending must be in the vehicle, awake, and not in the sleeper berth, or within 100 feet of the vehicle and have it within clear view.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-13

question: Near which of the following is it prohibited to use burning signals such as flares or fuses?
choice_a: A tank used for Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) or Division 2.1 (Flammable Gas), whether loaded or empty
choice_b: An empty flatbed trailer
choice_d: A vehicle carrying ORM-D materials
explanation: Never use burning signals, such as flares or fuses, around a tank used for Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) or Division 2.1 (Flammable Gas), whether loaded or empty, or a vehicle loaded with Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-14

question: When driving a placarded vehicle, what should you generally avoid unless there is no other way?
choice_a: Two-lane rural roads
choice_b: Rest areas
choice_d: Heavily populated areas, crowds, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys
explanation: Whenever placarded, avoid heavily populated areas, crowds, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys; take other routes, even if inconvenient, unless there is no other way.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-14

question: What must a driver transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives have and follow?
choice_a: A verbal agreement with dispatch only
choice_b: Nothing extra beyond the shipping papers
choice_d: A GPS unit with no other documentation
explanation: If transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, you must have a written route plan and follow that plan; carriers normally prepare it in advance and give the driver a copy.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-14

question: How close may a driver smoke to a placarded cargo tank used for Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) or Division 2.1 (Gases)?
choice_a: There is no distance restriction
choice_b: Smoking is prohibited within 25 feet
choice_c: Smoking is allowed if the windows are down
choice_d: Smoking is allowed 10 feet away
explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a placarded cargo tank used for Class 3 (flammable liquids) or Division 2.1 (gases).
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-14

question: When fueling a motor vehicle containing hazardous materials, what is required?
choice_a: Keep the engine running to power the pump
choice_b: Only the fuel attendant needs to be present, not the driver
choice_d: Turn off the engine and have someone at the nozzle controlling fuel flow
explanation: Turn off your engine before fueling a motor vehicle containing hazardous materials, and someone must always be at the nozzle, controlling fuel flow.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-14

question: What fire extinguisher rating must the power unit of a placarded vehicle have?
choice_a: A minimum of two 5-pound extinguishers of any rating
choice_b: A UL rating of 10 B:C or more
choice_c: A UL rating of 2 A:10 B:C or less
choice_d: No fire extinguisher is required if placarded for Class 9 only
explanation: The power unit of placarded vehicles must have a fire extinguisher with a UL rating of 10 B:C or more.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-14

question: A driver transporting chlorine in cargo tanks must have which special equipment in the vehicle?
choice_a: An extra set of shipping papers only
choice_b: A portable generator
choice_d: An approved gas mask and an emergency kit for controlling leaks in dome cover plate fittings
explanation: A driver transporting chlorine in cargo tanks must have an approved gas mask in the vehicle and an emergency kit for controlling leaks in dome cover plate fittings on the cargo tank.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-15

question: How far before the nearest rail must a driver of a placarded vehicle stop at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: 5 to 10 feet
choice_b: 100 to 150 feet
choice_d: 15 to 50 feet
explanation: You must stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail, proceeding only when sure no train is coming and you can clear the tracks without stopping.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-15

question: A carrier must give a driver transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives a copy of which regulation, along with written instructions on what to do if delayed or in an accident?
choice_a: OSHA's general industry standards
choice_b: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations (FMCSR), Part 397
choice_d: The state vehicle code, Title 28
explanation: A carrier must give each driver transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives a copy of FMCSR Part 397, plus written instructions on contacts, the nature of the explosives, and emergency precautions.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-15

question: As a driver at the scene of a hazardous materials crash or incident, what should you do?
choice_a: Keep people away from the scene and communicate the danger to emergency responders
choice_b: Move the vehicle to the nearest repair shop immediately
choice_c: Try to clean up the spill yourself before help arrives
choice_d: Wait inside the cab with the windows closed
explanation: Your job at the scene is to keep people away, limit the spread of material only if you can safely do so, communicate the danger to emergency responders, and provide shipping papers and emergency response information.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-15

question: If you discover your cargo is already on fire, what does the manual advise?
choice_a: Open all doors immediately to let smoke escape
choice_b: It is not safe to fight the fire; keep the shipping papers to give to emergency personnel
choice_c: Use water from a nearby source regardless of the material
choice_d: Continue driving to the nearest fire station
explanation: If cargo is already on fire, it is not safe to fight the fire; keep shipping papers with you to give to emergency personnel, and warn others to stay away.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-16

question: If you discover a hazardous materials leak, what should you avoid doing?
choice_a: Notifying your dispatcher
choice_b: Warning bystanders to stay away
choice_d: Touching the leaking material or trying to identify it by smell
explanation: Do not touch any leaking material, and do not try to identify the material or find the source of a leak by smell — toxic gases can destroy your sense of smell and can injure or kill you even if they don't smell.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-16

question: You or your employer must phone the National Response Center if, as a direct result of a hazardous materials incident, which of the following occurs?
choice_a: A person is killed, or estimated property damage exceeds $50,000
choice_b: The shipment is delivered one hour late
choice_c: The shipping paper has a minor spelling error
choice_d: The driver receives a parking ticket
explanation: The National Response Center must be notified when a person is killed, an injured person requires hospitalization, estimated property damage exceeds $50,000, or other listed triggers occur.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-16

question: What is CHEMTREC?
choice_a: A private insurance carrier for hazmat shipments
choice_b: A federal agency that issues CDL endorsements
choice_c: A 24-hour toll-free line that provides emergency personnel with technical information about the physical properties of hazardous materials
choice_d: The shipper's internal safety department
explanation: CHEMTREC, the Chemical Transportation Emergency Center in Washington, has a 24-hour toll-free line created to provide emergency personnel with technical information about the physical properties of hazardous materials.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 9 - Hazardous Materials, p. 9-17
